supersession_reason: The v1 receipt became historical under its own change_control rule: RESULTS_LEDGER.json, notes/MEDGUARD_MASTER_EXECUTION_PLAN.md and notes/TARGETS_TO_BEAT.md all changed after it was created. v1 and its receipt are preserved byte-identical and must never be edited: five frozen artifacts pin the v1 receipt hash 5a990ece1c41b21d491b4919b5f31817c1522306846fbcd0058c84d1a05bbfd8.
hash_convention: SHA-256 of raw file bytes exactly as stored
source_tree_revision_note: v1 recorded this as pending because .git existed but was an empty directory and git rev-parse reported not a git repository. medguard/.env was excluded before the first commit and is absent from all history. The exact revision for any run is recorded by that run, not by this receipt; this value states when the repository became pinnable.
two_tier_rationale: v1 pinned the results ledger and the working notes with the same force as the specification, so ordinary appends and edits silently invalidated it -- which is exactly how it died. A ledger that is append-only by design and notes that are meant to evolve cannot be design-binding without guaranteeing false breakage. Splitting the tiers keeps the freeze meaningful: design_binding_files must not change without a version bump, while observed_files are recorded for provenance and are expected to drift.
design_binding_rule: These carry the freeze. If any one changes, this receipt becomes historical: issue v3 and state the reason. Never edit a version in place after viewing current-paper results.
observed_rule: Recorded for provenance at receipt creation. Drift is expected and does not invalidate this receipt. RESULTS_LEDGER.json is append-only; the notes evolve with the work; the implementation cards are a declared living_prelock_specification. The cards become design-binding at the pre-H2H lock and must be re-pinned into design_binding_files at that point.
authorization: This receipt freezes the design only. It does not authorize paid generation or sealed-test access.
